- Invoice adjustments: we can issue a credit note for material shortfalls but require proof of deduction (bank confirmation) and the PO/invoice reference.

Emma — Laura from Billing here. Quick operational guidance and the path we recommend:

1) Routing: ask your bank to send as OUR. If they need a contractual statement, Redwood confirms that the beneficiary account (Redwood Inference Europe Ltd as per redwood_eu_account_stub.pdf) is correct and that Redwood prefers payments to arrive gross. We will acknowledge receipt and refund/credit only in cases where fees are deducted despite an OUR instruction (we cannot retroactively force a bank to reimburse correspondent charges).

2) Shortfalls and credits: if the payer cannot send OUR and the incoming amount is short, please provide the bank trace and deduction amount. We will open a reconciliation case and, where valid, issue a credit note tied to INV-4521. Credits will reflect the gross shortfall amount (no additional VAT will be added by Redwood on the credit itself — credits will reduce the taxable base on the original invoice).

3) VAT: since ACME Health UK Ltd supplied a UK VAT ID (GB987654321), and this is a B2B cross-border transaction between a UK company and an EU-registered supplier (Redwood Inference Europe Ltd), standard reverse-charge treatment applies for VAT purposes. That means Redwood will issue the invoice without charging VAT and will include ACME's VAT ID on the invoice; ACME will self-account for VAT in the UK if applicable. If the payer is ultimately a non-EU/US treasury entity, please let us know as VAT rules will differ.

Action items for ACME / PayBridge:
- Confirm they can set OUR or confirm that they will accept the alternative workflow (we'll reconcile any deductions post-payment).
- Share the exact legal invoice-to entity (you provided ACME Health UK Ltd — we'll use that on the invoice).
- Provide the PO number so we can append it to the remittance and final invoice lines.
